'''Alar Karis''' ({{IPA|et|ˈɑlɑr ˈkɑris|est}}; born 26 March 1958) is an [[Estonia]]n scientist ([[Molecular genetics|molecular geneticist]] and [[Developmental biology|developmental biologist]]), civil servant<ref name="ETIS">{{Cite web|title=CV: Alar Karis|url=https://www.etis.ee/CV/Alar_Karis|access-date=13 March 2021|website=www.etis.ee}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Tambur|first=Silver|date=2021-08-31|title=Alar Karis elected president of Estonia|url=https://estonianworld.com/life/alar-karis-elected-president-of-estonia/|access-date=2021-08-31|website=Estonian World|language=en-GB}}</ref> and politician who served as the sixth [[president of Estonia]] from 11 October 2021 to 12 October 2026.

== Prior to presidency ==
Karis was born in [[Tartu]] on 26 March 1958.<ref name=ETIS/><ref name=":02">{{Cite web|date=2021-08-30|title=Who is Estonia's next president Alar Karis?|url=https://news.err.ee/1608321551/who-is-estonia-s-next-president-alar-karis|access-date=2021-08-31|website=ERR|language=en}}</ref> He was raised there by his mother and grandmother after his parents divorced in 1960.<ref>{{cite web |title=Presidendi Sugupuu Kuidas mustlased väikese Alar Karise Tartu turult ära varastasid |url=https://ekspress.delfi.ee/artikkel/95492615/presidendi-sugupuu-kuidas-mustlased-vaikese-alar-karise-tartu-turult-ara-varastasid |publisher=Eesti Ekspress |access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref>

In 1981, he graduated from the [[Estonian Agricultural Academy]] (now renamed [[Estonian University of Life Sciences]]) in Tartu.<ref name=":02" /> In 1987, he received the degree of [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate of Veterinary Sciences]] from the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus|Academy of Sciences of the Byelorussian SSR]] in [[Minsk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rus.delfi.ee/statja/120437042/alar-karis-zashchishchal-nauchnuyu-stepen-v-minske-v-oficialnyh-biografiyah-na-estonskom-yazyke-eto-ne-upominaetsya|title=Алар Карис защищал научную степень в Минске. В официальных биографиях на эстонском языке это не упоминается|website=[[Delfi (web portal)|Delfi]]|date=18 February 2026|language=Russian}}</ref> In 1999, he became a professor at the [[University of Tartu]].<ref name=":02" />

Karis served as [[rector (academia)|rector]] of the Estonian University of Life Sciences from 2003 to 2007, as [[rector of Tartu University|rector]] of the University of Tartu from 2007 to 2012, as the [[Auditor General of Estonia]] from 2013 to 2018, and as director of the [[Estonian National Museum]] from 2018 to 2021.<ref name=ETIS/><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2021-08-19|title=Potential presidential candidate: Smart and educated nation key to future|url=https://news.err.ee/1608312020/potential-presidential-candidate-smart-and-educated-nation-key-to-future|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-22|website=ERR|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210819060830/https://news.err.ee/1608312020/potential-presidential-candidate-smart-and-educated-nation-key-to-future |archive-date=19 August 2021 }}</ref>

== President of Estonia (2021–2026) ==
[[File:Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Estonian President Karis in Kyiv 2022 (5).jpg|thumb|Karis meets with Ukrainian President [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] in Kyiv two days before the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]], on 22 February 2022]]
In August 2021, he was approached by the speaker of the parliament ([[Riigikogu]]) [[Jüri Ratas]] with a prospect of nomination for the position of the president of Estonia in the [[2021 Estonian presidential election|upcoming election]] in the autumn.<ref>{{Cite web|date=17 August 2021|title=Riigikogu speaker asks museum director to consider running as president|url=https://news.err.ee/1608309632/riigikogu-speaker-asks-museum-director-to-consider-running-as-president|url-status=live|access-date=22 August 2021|website=ERR|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817102117/https://news.err.ee/1608309632/riigikogu-speaker-asks-museum-director-to-consider-running-as-president |archive-date=17 August 2021 }}</ref> He accepted the nomination<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-18|title=Museum director says 'yes' in answer to presidential bid offer|url=https://news.err.ee/1608310604/museum-director-says-yes-in-answer-to-presidential-bid-offer|url-status=live|access-date=22 August 2021|website=ERR|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818173908/https://news.err.ee/1608310604/museum-director-says-yes-in-answer-to-presidential-bid-offer |archive-date=18 August 2021 }}</ref> and his candidacy was subsequently endorsed by both coalition parties, the [[Estonian Reform Party|Reform Party]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-19|title=Reform Party Riigikogu group supports Karis as presidential candidate|url=https://news.err.ee/1608312419/reform-party-riigikogu-group-supports-karis-as-presidential-candidate|access-date=22 August 2021|website=ERR|language=en}}</ref> and the [[Estonian Centre Party|Centre Party]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=22 August 2021|title=Center joins Reform in support for Alar Karis presidential candidacy|url=https://news.err.ee/1608314117/center-joins-reform-in-support-for-alar-karis-presidential-candidacy|url-status=live|access-date=22 August 2021|website=ERR|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210822120422/https://news.err.ee/1608314117/center-joins-reform-in-support-for-alar-karis-presidential-candidacy |archive-date=22 August 2021 }}</ref> On 31 August 2021, Karis was elected as the president of Estonia with a two thirds majority of 72 votes in the Riigikogu.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=31 August 2021|title=Alar Karis elected President of Estonia|url=https://news.err.ee/1608321953/alar-karis-elected-president-of-estonia|access-date=31 August 2021|website=ERR|language=en}}</ref> He assumed the office on 11 October 2021.<ref name=":1" />
[[File:Carl XVI Gustaf ja Alar Karis Tallinnas (2023).jpg|thumb|Karis with King [[Carl XVI Gustaf]] of Sweden in Tallinn, 2 May 2023]]
The election received criticism and calls for electoral reform due to the absence of opposing candidates.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-30|title=Estonia on presidential election day as Karis stays sole candidate|url=https://bnn-news.com/estonia-on-presidential-election-day-as-karis-stays-sole-candidate-227834|access-date=8 January 2022|website=Baltic News Network - News from Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-28|title=Estonia faces prospect of an election with only one candidate|url=https://www.euronews.com/2021/08/28/30-years-after-soviet-rule-ended-estonia-faces-an-election-with-a-single-candidate|access-date=8 January 2022|website=euronews|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Tanner|first=Jari|date=2021-08-28|title=Only one candidate in Estonia presidential election|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/only-one-candidate-in-estonia-presidential-election/|access-date=8 January 2022|website=CTVNews|language=en}}</ref> In his acceptance speech Karis referenced the "turmoil that surrounded the presidential selection process" and called for changes of the system to be examined by the Riigikogu, such as using an enlarged electoral college, facilitating the nomination of candidates or even using direct election. He promised to be a balancer and a mediator during his presidential term.<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 October 2021|title=Karis: I intend to be a balancer above all, and if necessary, a mediator|url=https://news.err.ee/1608366507/karis-i-intend-to-be-a-balancer-above-all-and-if-necessary-a-mediator|access-date=2022-01-08|website=ERR|language=en}}</ref>

[[File:UN AI for Good Summit 2025 - Alar Karis 01 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Karis at the 2025 [[ITU AI for Good|AI for Good Summit]] in [[Geneva]]]]

Karis started his presidency with state visits to Latvia and Finland.<ref>{{cite web |title=Karis to visit Latvia, Finland on Thursday |url=https://news.err.ee/1608366351/karis-to-visit-latvia-finland-on-thursday |website=ERR |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en |date=11 October 2021}}</ref> The visit to Latvia was hosted by the [[speaker of the Saeima]] [[Ināra Mūrniece]] as President of Latvia [[Egils Levits]] had tested positive for [[COVID-19]] the previous evening.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alar Karise esimese välisvisiidi ajakava muutus, kuna Läti riigipea nakatus koroonasse |url=https://www.delfi.ee/artikkel/94851623/alar-karise-esimese-valisvisiidi-ajakava-muutus-kuna-lati-riigipea-nakatus-koroonasse |website=Delfi |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=et}}</ref>

Karis on several occasions has used his right not to promulgate laws passed by the parliament. In December 2023 Karis refused to promulgate a law due to finding that the rules of proceedings were violated by the government by tying the bill to confidence vote. Karis found in his decision that all-out obstruction in the Riigikogu, that may render the parliament unable to work, does not give the government the right to keep tying all bills to confidence votes and therefore pushing them through the parliament.<ref>{{cite web |title=President refuses to promulgate a law due to rules of proceedings violation |url=https://news.err.ee/1609189276/president-refuses-to-promulgate-a-law-due-to-rules-of-proceedings-violation |website=ERR |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en |date=8 December 2023}}</ref> The Riigikogu however adopted the bill unchanged, Karis refused to promulgate the second time and sent the bill to the [[Supreme Court of Estonia|Supreme Court]].<ref>{{cite web |title=President sends Land Tax amendments to Supreme Court |work=ERR |url=https://news.err.ee/1609211030/president-sends-land-tax-amendments-to-supreme-court |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en |date=3 January 2024}}</ref> Supreme Court sided with Karis.<ref>{{cite web |title=Riigikohus: valitsus ei tohi piiramatult eelnõusid usaldusküsimusega siduda |url=https://www.err.ee/1609317084/riigikohus-valitsus-ei-tohi-piiramatult-eelnousid-usalduskusimusega-siduda |website=ERR |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=et |date=18 April 2024}}</ref>

In July 2024 Karis did not proclaim the Vehicle Tax Act finding it to be unconstitutional in violating the principle of equal treatment in the part that deals with persons with disabilities.<ref>{{cite web |title=President Karis decides not to promulgate Estonia's car tax law |url=https://news.err.ee/1609380878/president-karis-decides-not-to-promulgate-estonia-s-car-tax-law |website=ERR |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en |date=25 June 2024}}</ref> He approved it when the law was amended by the parliament.<ref>{{cite web |title=President promulgates vehicle tax law |url=https://news.err.ee/1609420852/president-promulgates-vehicle-tax-law |website=ERR |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en |date=9 August 2024}}</ref>

On 23 June 2026, Karis announced during his [[Võidupüha|Estonian Victory Day]] address in [[Rapla]] that he would not seek a second term in the [[2026 Estonian presidential election]]. Stating that his decision was for personal reasons, he cited a prior agreement made with his family to serve only a single term.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-23 |title=President Alar Karis will not run for second presidential term |url=https://news.err.ee/1610061664/president-alar-karis-will-not-run-for-second-presidential-term |access-date=2026-08-02 |website=ERR |language=en}}</ref> Opposition leaders from the [[Estonian Centre Party|Centre Party]] and [[Isamaa]] subsequently claimed that Karis was pressured into the decision by the governing coalition despite high public approval ratings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tambur |first=Silver |date=2026-06-23 |title=Estonia’s president Alar Karis says he will not seek a second term |url=https://estonianworld.com/life/estonias-president-alar-karis-says-he-will-not-seek-a-second-term/ |access-date=2026-08-02 |website=Estonian World |language=en-GB}}</ref> Estonian daily [[Postimees]] pointed to his tenure as a "one-term man", citing his decisions to serve one term in previous offices as well.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-09 |title=JUHTKIRI &#10217; Kuuenda presidendi viis aastat |url=https://arvamus.postimees.ee/8561829/juhtkiri-kuuenda-presidendi-viis-aastat |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=Arvamus |language=et}}</ref>

He left the office of president on 12 October 2026, being succeeded by [[Ülle Madise]].

==Personal life==
His father was the [[botanist]] Harry Karis (1930–2018)<ref>''Eesti Entsüklopeedia 14'', p. 142. Tallinn 2000. ISBN 9985-70-064-3 (in Estonian)</ref> and his mother Virve Karis (1928–2020), an agriculture specialist in animal nutrition.<ref>{{cite web |title=Virve Karis in memoriam |url=https://agrt.emu.ee/pdf/chronicle/2020_1_kart.pdf |publisher=Estonian University of Life Sciences |access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref> He grew up with his mother and grandmother Vilhelmine after his parents divorced in 1960.

He has been married to [[Sirje Karis]] (née Jädal) since 1977, with whom he has 3 children and 5 grandchildren.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-24 |title=First lady Sirje Karis not planning on moving out of Tartu home yet |url=https://news.err.ee/1608349574/first-lady-sirje-karis-not-planning-on-moving-out-of-tartu-home-yet |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=ERR |language=en}}</ref> Besides [[Estonian language|Estonian]], Karis is fluent in [[English language|English]] and [[Russian language|Russian]]. Although he is fluent in Russian, he has admitted that it needs some practice since he has not had to speak the language in a long time.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.delfi.ee/artikkel/94478103/video-vaata-kuidas-saab-eesti-valitud-president-hakkama-venekeelsete-kusimustega | title=VIDEO &#124; Vaata, kuidas saab Eesti valitud president hakkama venekeelsete küsimustega }}</ref>
